lesson_scope: Vector and Cartesian equations of planes, finding normal vectors via scalar product ratios and cross products, perpendicular bisector planes, planes containing lines and points, intersecting/perpendicular planes, and pyramid sloping face plane equations with dihedral angles.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Direct Cartesian plane equation from normal and point.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Direct plane equation from normal vector and point.

hints: Write the general Cartesian form $ax + by + cz = d$ using normal coefficients $2x - 3y + 5z = d$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the normal coefficients from $\mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -3 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$:
$$2x - 3y + 5z = d$$

Substitute coordinates of point $A(1, 4, 2)$ to calculate constant $d$:
$$d = 2(1) - 3(4) + 5(2) = 2 - 12 + 10 = 0$$

State the Cartesian equation of the plane:
$$2x - 3y + 5z = 0$$

hints: Parallel planes share the same normal vector, so keep the coefficients $x + 4y - 8z = d$.

walkthrough.text:
Parallel planes have identical normal vectors, so write the equation as:
$$x + 4y - 8z = d$$

Substitute coordinates of point $P(5, 2, -2)$ to find $d$:
$$d = 5 + 4(2) - 8(-2) = 5 + 8 + 16 = 29$$

State the Cartesian equation:
$$x + 4y - 8z = 29$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Normal vector ratio solving from two scalar product equations.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Normal vector ratios from scalar products.

hints: Substitute into $a - 2b + 3c = 0 \implies a - 2(2a + c) + 3c = 0 \implies -3a + c = 0 \implies c = 3a$.
Substitute $c = 3a$ into $b$: $b = 2a + 3a = 5a$. The ratio is $a : b : c = 1 : 5 : 3$, so $\mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 5 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$.

walkthrough.text:
Express $b$ in terms of $a$ and $c$ from the second equation:
$$2a - b + c = 0 \implies b = 2a + c$$

Substitute into the first equation to express $c$ in terms of $a$:
$$a - 2(2a + c) + 3c = 0 \implies a - 4a - 2c + 3c = 0 \implies -3a + c = 0 \implies c = 3a$$

Express $b$ in terms of $a$ and state the integer normal vector:
$$b = 2a + 3a = 5a$$
$$a : b : c = 1 : 5 : 3 \implies \mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 5 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute the coordinates of midpoint $M$:
$$M = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix} 3 + (-1) \\ 4 + 0 \\ 0 + 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute the normal vector from segment $AB$:
$$\vec{BA} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 - (-1) \\ 4 - 0 \\ 0 - 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 4 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix} = 2\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} \implies \mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Evaluate constant $d$ and state the Cartesian equation:
$$d = 2(1) + 2(2) - 1(1) = 2 + 4 - 1 = 5 \implies 2x + 2y - z = 5$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Vector to Cartesian plane conversion and point test.

hints: Since $12 = 12$, confirm that $P$ lies on the plane.

walkthrough.text:
Expand the vector equation into Cartesian form:
$$\mathbf{r} \cdot \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -1 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} = 12 \implies 3x - y + 4z = 12$$

Substitute coordinates of point $P(2, 2, 2)$:
$$3(2) - 2 + 4(2) = 6 - 2 + 8 = 12$$
Since $12 = 12$, point $P$ lies on the plane.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Vector cross product normal calculation.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the determinant formula for the cross product $\mathbf{u} \times \mathbf{v}$:
$$\mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} (1)(5) - (0)(0) \\ (0)(1) - (2)(5) \\ (2)(0) - (1)(1) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -10 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Core: Plane through three points in space.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the displacement vectors from vertex $A(1, 3, 2)$:
$$\vec{AB} = \mathbf{b} - \mathbf{a} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 - 1 \\ 1 - 3 \\ -1 - 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$\vec{AC} = \mathbf{c} - \mathbf{a} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 - 1 \\ 4 - 3 \\ 1 - 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$

parts.label: (b)

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Cartesian plane equation from three points.

hints: Solve $a - 2b - 3c = 0$ and $a + b - c = 0 \implies 3b + 2c = 0 \implies b = -\frac{2}{3}c, a = \frac{5}{3}c$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up scalar product equations with normal $\mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} a \\ b \\ c \end{pmatrix}$:
$$a - 2b - 3c = 0 \quad \text{--- (1)}$$
$$a + b - c = 0 \quad \text{--- (2)}$$
Subtract (1) from (2): $3b + 2c = 0 \implies b = -\frac{2}{3}c$
Substitute into (2): $a - \frac{2}{3}c - c = 0 \implies a = \frac{5}{3}c$
$$\mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -2 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$$

Evaluate constant $d$ using point $A(1, 3, 2)$:
$$d = 5(1) - 2(3) + 3(2) = 5 - 6 + 6 = 5$$
The Cartesian equation is $5x - 2y + 3z = 5$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Core: Plane containing two intersecting lines.

walkthrough.text:
Set up orthogonality equations for the normal $\mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} a \\ b \\ c \end{pmatrix}$:
$$\mathbf{n} \cdot \mathbf{d}_1 = a - 2b + 3c = 0 \quad \text{--- (1)}$$
$$\mathbf{n} \cdot \mathbf{d}_2 = 2a - b + c = 0 \quad \text{--- (2)}$$

Solve for the ratios:
$$b = 2a + c \implies a - 2(2a + c) + 3c = 0 \implies -3a + c = 0 \implies c = 3a$$
$$b = 2a + 3a = 5a \implies a : b : c = 1 : 5 : 3$$
$$\mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 5 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up equations in $a, b, c$.

parts.label: (b)
hints: Use the common point of intersection $(2, 1, 2)$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute the point $(2, 1, 2)$ into the Cartesian form $x + 5y + 3z = d$:
$$d = 1(2) + 5(1) + 3(2) = 2 + 5 + 6 = 13$$

State the Cartesian equation of the plane:
$$x + 5y + 3z = 13$$

Compute the midpoint $M$:
$$M = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix} 3 + (-1) \\ 4 + 0 \\ 0 + 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute the displacement vector $\vec{AB}$:
$$\vec{AB} = \begin{pmatrix} -1 - 3 \\ 0 - 4 \\ 2 - 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ -4 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$$

Identify the normal vector $\mathbf{n}$ perpendicular to the bisector plane:
$$\mathbf{n} = \vec{BA} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 4 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix} = 2\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} \implies \mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Substitute the midpoint coordinates $M(1, 2, 1)$ into $2x + 2y - z = d$:
$$d = 2(1) + 2(2) - 1(1) = 2 + 4 - 1 = 5$$

Conclude the plane equation:
$$2x + 2y - z = 5$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Core: Plane equation from 3 points with negative constant.

walkthrough.text:
Compute displacement vectors $\vec{CB}$ and $\vec{CD}$:
$$\vec{CB} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 - (-1) \\ 2 - 1 \\ 3 - 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$\vec{CD} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 - (-1) \\ 1 - 1 \\ 8 - 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute normal vector $\mathbf{n}$:
$$\mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 - 0 \\ 0 - 10 \\ 0 - 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -10 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up cross product or scalar equations.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Cartesian plane equation with constant evaluation.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute coordinates of point $B(1, 2, 3)$ into $5x - 10y - z = d$:
$$d = 5(1) - 10(2) - 1(3) = 5 - 20 - 3 = -18$$

State the Cartesian equation:
$$5x - 10y - z = -18$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Capstone: Plane containing a line and external point with full identity proof.

parts.label: (a)

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Line and external point plane directions.

hints: Displacement from base point $A(1, 0, 2)$ to $P(3, 2, 1)$ is $\mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$.
Solve $2a + b - c = 0$ and $2a + 2b - c = 0 \implies b = 0, c = 2a \implies \mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify two independent direction vectors lying in plane $\Pi$:
$$\mathbf{u} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{p} - \mathbf{a} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 - 1 \\ 2 - 0 \\ 1 - 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Find the normal vector $\mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} a \\ b \\ c \end{pmatrix}$:
$$2a + b - c = 0 \quad \text{--- (1)}$$
$$2a + 2b - c = 0 \quad \text{--- (2)}$$
Subtract (1) from (2): $b = 0 \implies 2a - c = 0 \implies c = 2a$
$$\mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$$

parts.label: (b)
hints: Using normal $(1, 0, 2)$ and point $P(3, 2, 1)$, calculate $d = 1(3) + 0(2) + 2(1) = 5 \implies x + 2z = 5$.
Substitute line $l$ coordinates $x = 1 + 2\lambda, y = \lambda, z = 2 - \lambda$ into $x + 2z$.
Evaluate $(1 + 2\lambda) + 2(2 - \lambda) = 1 + 2\lambda + 4 - 2\lambda = 5$. Since this equals $5$ identically for all $\lambda$, the line lies on the plane.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute coordinates of point $P(3, 2, 1)$ into $x + 2z = d$:
$$d = 1(3) + 0(2) + 2(1) = 5 \implies x + 2z = 5$$

Verify that the general point of line $l$ satisfies the plane equation identically:
$$\mathbf{r}(\lambda) = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + 2\lambda \\ \lambda \\ 2 - \lambda \end{pmatrix}$$
$$\text{LHS} = x + 2z = (1 + 2\lambda) + 2(2 - \lambda) = 1 + 2\lambda + 4 - 2\lambda = 5$$
Since $\text{LHS} = 5$ for all values of parameter $\lambda$, the entire line $l$ lies on the plane.

questions.difficulty_reason: Capstone: Perpendicular planes proof and line of intersection derivation.

parts.label: (a)
hints: Conclude that the planes are perpendicular.

walkthrough.text:
Extract the normal vectors of both planes:
$$\mathbf{n}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{n}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute their scalar product:
$$\mathbf{n}_1 \cdot \mathbf{n}_2 = 2(1) + (-1)(3) + 1(1) = 2 - 3 + 1 = 0$$
Since $\mathbf{n}_1 \cdot \mathbf{n}_2 = 0$, the normal vectors are perpendicular, proving that the planes $\Pi_1$ and $\Pi_2$ are perpendicular.

parts.label: (b)

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Line of intersection of two planes.

hints: Find a point on the line: set $z = 0 \implies 2x - y = 3$ and $x + 3y = 7$.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the direction vector of the line of intersection via the cross product of the plane normals:
$$\mathbf{d} = \mathbf{n}_1 \times \mathbf{n}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -1 - 3 \\ 1 - 2 \\ 6 - (-1) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ -1 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix} \sim \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 1 \\ -7 \end{pmatrix}$$

Find a particular point on the intersection line by setting $z = 0$:
$$2x - y = 3 \quad \text{--- (1)}$$
$$x + 3y = 7 \implies x = 7 - 3y \quad \text{--- (2)}$$
$$2(7 - 3y) - y = 3 \implies 14 - 7y = 3 \implies 7y = 11 \implies y = \frac{11}{7}$$
(Or let $y = 1 \implies 2x - 1 + z = 3 \implies 2x + z = 4$, and $x + 3 + z = 7 \implies x + z = 4 \implies x = 0, z = 4 \implies (0, 1, 4)$).

Check point $(0, 1, 4)$:
$$\Pi_1: 2(0) - 1 + 4 = 3$$
$$\Pi_2: 0 + 3(1) + 4 = 7$$
State the vector equation of the intersection line:
$$\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} + \lambda \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 1 \\ -7 \end{pmatrix}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Solves for a common point on both planes.

questions.difficulty_reason: Capstone: Pyramid sloping face plane equations and dihedral angle.

walkthrough.text:
Compute displacement vectors in face plane $VAB$ from vertex $A(0, 0, 0)$:
$$\vec{AB} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} \sim \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \vec{AV} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix} \sim \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute normal vector $\mathbf{n}$:
$$\mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ -3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} \sim \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Evaluate constant $d$ using $A(0, 0, 0)$:
$$3(0) - 1(0) = 0 \implies 3y - z = 0$$

Compute displacement vectors in face $VCD$ from $D(0, 4, 0)$:
$$\vec{DC} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} \sim \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \vec{DV} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -2 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix} \sim \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute normal vector $\mathbf{n}$:
$$\mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ -3 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} \sim \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Evaluate constant $d$ using $D(0, 4, 0)$:
$$d = 3(4) + 1(0) = 12 \implies 3y + z = 12$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Dihedral angle between face plane and base plane.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the normal vectors to the face plane and base plane:
$$\mathbf{n}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{n}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute the scalar product and magnitudes:
$$\mathbf{n}_1 \cdot \mathbf{n}_2 = 0(0) + 3(0) + (-1)(1) = -1$$
$$|\mathbf{n}_1| = \sqrt{0^2 + 3^2 + (-1)^2} = \sqrt{10}, \quad |\mathbf{n}_2| = 1$$

Calculate the acute dihedral angle $\theta$:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{|\mathbf{n}_1 \cdot \mathbf{n}_2|}{|\mathbf{n}_1| |\mathbf{n}_2|} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{10} \times 1} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}$$
$$\theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\right) \approx 71.6^\circ$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies base normal and face normal.
